responseFromOwnerText:
Thanks for the rating and comments / feedback; it is important for us to improve and maintain our service quality. We have four time slots (10:30AM-12:30PM, 1-3PM, 3:30-5:30PM and 6-8PM) on weekends and holidays. Every two hours of the operation on busy weekends & holidays, we take a 15 mins break for cleaning so that a clean facility can be presented to our guests in the next time slot. During the other 15 mins, which is a transition period when guests of the ended party are leaving and guests of the new parties in the following time slots are checking in.

Please note: 0n weekdays, we do not take such breaks due to the low traffic and that is why cleaning is done in parallel.

text:
Very unclear about the policy. Booked a party. On that same day they got demanding and pushy stating "the deposit had to be made ASAP in one day" and is "non refundable" so I went ahead and paid the deposit. While looking into options they kept texting the package includes parents and kids "altogether" not clarifying what that meant after multiple texts. I asked for clear clarification please. They sent me a text stating that for 30 kids, I could choose the package for 30 and if the number came to 50 for example with parents included I'd pay the 30 "package" when the remaining balance is due. There were options for 20, 30, or more depending on my number which I needed to confirm by a set date once I received the rsvp and at that time pay the remaining amount. Of course I needed to send invites and confirm the amount which I did. When the date came to indicate how many people rsvpd and pay the remaining balance they started texting again and changing. Sounding unclear again. They asked is that 20 "altogether?" I tried to get information and clarify. I also reminded what they had already texted to me initially and understood from that initial text to mean Id pay for the kids (the 20 package for the 14 kids attending) and a parent could bring them. I basically was just trying to understand what their policy was and what "altogether" meant so I could get the correct package. They would not clearly tell me leaving me confused as to what package option. The "booking department" randomly then texted "maybe you should just cancel" suggesting to cancel the whole party. This was after learning and knowing that my guests had already been invited, rsvp'd, and planned on atending with remaining balance due the next day (as planned). They insisted on sending texts only. Would not communicate over the phone or in person at all. I tried calling. No answer. After that they sent me another text different from the initial agreement "the package that includes 20 people" would require parents that bring their kids to be charged each an extra $15 on top of the package price if they bring their kid to the party. I was confused. I said that is not what they initially agreed/texted me but it will be fine, and in that case I guess I could also ask parents to wait outside in their car since it would be $15 extra to bring their children that I was not made aware of initially. I said they would likely understand. After that they then texted back again saying "that's not what they said" and that parents in fact could bring their kids to the party and would "not be charged" for doing so. I reconfirmed for like the 5th time I would send the remainder amount based on the14 kids and pay the remainder by tomorrow as preplanned. Then immediately after I texted that that they then texted back "The party has been canceled and you will receive your deposit shortly" I replied why?.. people have already rsvpd from school and some by mouth and this will create much difficulty at this point. They couldnt care less. Absolutely 💯 stressful and crazy experience and would not suggest doing business with these people unless you are for certain this type of thing won't happen again. Make sure you get some safeguards in writing for your event. Don't just text back and forth with these people. No response to that request at all, or options to speak over the phone or in person. Very odd way of doing business.

text:
The actual play space at Kid’s Playtown is great — it’s colorful, creative, and kept the kids entertained for a good while. My child had a blast, and it’s clearly designed to be engaging and fun. That said, there were a few broken toys and features, which made parts of it feel a bit run-down or not well-maintained.

The party rooms were underwhelming — very basic and didn’t add much to the experience.

What really brought the experience down for me was the pricing and the overall business setup. Admission is $15 per child, but they also charge $10 per adult — which is odd considering there’s no staff actively watching or managing the kids. Adults are the ones supervising, so you end up paying the business to watch your own child, which just doesn’t sit right.

On top of that, they ask for an e-transfer in advance just to reserve a spot, which felt a bit off. It’s not the most professional or transparent booking system, and honestly came across as a little sketchy.

All in all, the kids might have fun, but for the price and the setup, it’s hard to fully recommend. If they cleaned up the space, improved their booking process, and reconsidered the adult fee, it could be a much better experience.
responseFromOwnerText:
Hello Sam
Thank you for the review and visiting Playtown.
A lot of people like our party rooms and it is just about personal preferences. If you are just visiting for the playtime slot, party rooms are not part of the playground experience anyway.
Pricing is mentioned on the website along with the terms and conditions. It is $5 for the adults and not $10 if you are coming with more than one child.
Playtown is an unsupervised playground and parents are to monitor their children at all times as we are not a daycare or a baby sitting service. It is clearly mentioned on our website and in the booking details that were sent to you at the time of booking.
A lot of facilities charge in advance as suited, based on the structure and requirements of the business. We do take etransfer payments to confirm the booking and it is mentioned in the booking details before you decide to make the payment so it does not come as a surprise. This booking method streamlines and makes the transaction prompt; eliminating the wait times at the entrance.
When children are playing naturally the playground gets messy just as it would get messy at your own home or place of residence and gets cleaned up after they are done playing. Same rules apply everywhere. We keep up with the cleanup and close between the slots to clean and reorganize.

Hope this helps.
Thank you again for visiting Playtown :)

text:
Our experience with KidStrong was very disappointing, especially as parents of a child on the autism spectrum. The program did not feel inclusive or supportive of children who may need additional encouragement or a different approach.
During the classes, we noticed that children who were already stronger or more capable were praised and rewarded, while children who struggled were often left behind. In one instance, a prize was given to the child who performed the best, which only reinforced the feeling that the program focuses on children who can already excel rather than helping every child progress at their own pace.
We explained that our child was not fitting into the group environment and that the program did not appear appropriate for his needs. Despite this, we were told that we were committed to a one-year agreement and they continued charging us rather than working with us on a reasonable cancellation or refund.
For families with children on the spectrum or other special needs, I would strongly recommend asking very detailed questions before signing a long-term contract. Based on our experience, this program seemed much better suited to children who can easily participate in a competitive group environment. Children who need additional support may end up feeling left behind instead of encouraged.
What bothered us most was not that our child struggled—it was the lack of flexibility and understanding once it became clear that the program was not a good fit.
responseFromOwnerText:
We’re sincerely sorry to hear about this experience. However, we’re unable to identify you as a member of KidStrong Burlington, and this same review appears to have been posted to several independently owned locations. KidStrong Burlington does not offer one-year membership commitments.

Our program is designed for children who can participate in a group class with some independence. When a child needs additional support, our team works with the family on strategies and may invite a parent or guardian onto the floor to help them adjust. If a child’s diagnosed needs made the program unsuitable, we would work with the family rather than hold them to a long-term commitment.

Again, we’re sorry this was your experience and wish your family all the best.

I was there yesterday with my toddler and my infant who is only 4 months old and i needed to use the washroom to change both diapers but they didn’t allow the double stroller inside. I asked them what do moms do who have two kids they said they can give me a high chair for the infant while I’m in the washroom. I explained to them that my 4 months old cannot sit in a high chair since she cannot lift her head up. They said I should bring the car seat and put her in the car seat on the floor. I explained to them that my double stroller has two seats (toddler seat and bassinet) and that the car seat is for the car as it’s not healthy to keep the infants in the car seats in the malls for their back and I need to use the washroom too so I need both kids strapped safely in my stroller. They said they will ask the manager. After over half an hour they didn’t come back with an answer but rather asked me to go speak to the manager. After so much back and forth with the manager they agreed to clean my stroller’s wheels with wipes and allowed me to take the double stroller to the washroom. They asked me to bring the car seat next time which doesn’t solve my problem.
I’m just wondering how no one has ever had an issue with bringing two kids to this place.. it was very inconvenient.
responseFromOwnerText:
Hi Yusur,

I am so sorry for yesterday. I am a twin mom myself and I understand the dilemma with two small kids. As a playplace for young kids the full area where kids play and the lobby to walk is carpeted and as a mom you know the babies/toddlers are crawling, can pick things from the floor. Moms also many times sit with blankets on the floor while nursing the babies. To keep it hygienic and clean, we are very particular on no shoes on the carpet or any kind of wheels. The strollers unfortunately can’t go inside. Only car seats. In emergency like yours yesterday the team does clean the wheels with wipes.

Hope this helps to understand from our perspective.

Take care and blessings…..Neetu

text:
Love the offerings at the Activity Plex - no complaints about the individual businesses, however the ActivityPlex itself is in desperate need of some TLC.

The floor is warped in multiple areas, which can cause people to trip. The building isn’t that old, so it shouldn’t be in such rough shape, and yet it is. I’ve never seen a maintenance person, cleaning person, or any person who works for the ActivityPlex at all in all the years we’ve been coming here, which seems strange given there is a definite need for maintenance and/or cleaning during the peak times. (Especially during winter, when the vestibule floors and mats are soaked with dirty water and salt.)

The red and black couches in the sitting area and in the hallway are FILTHY with stains, dirt, spills, etc. They badly need a professional steam clean and proper stain/spill resistant treatment. They look like they’ve never, ever been cleaned. Ever. Please, clean them immediately. Please.

The parking situation is a headache. As other reviewers have said, the main issue seems to be multiple vehicles per family. Each business within the activity plex needs to communicate to its membership base that only one car per family is allowed. The other day a family showed up in 4-5 different cars to watch one child swim for 30 minutes! I understand grandparents may want to attend, but it should be occasional, and carpooling is absolutely necessary. The ActivityPlex should enforce a one-vehicle limit (understanding there are limited situations where an additional vehicle is needed). Adding numbers to parking spots and creating a parking app where families have to register their vehicles & book a time slot for a parking spot could help better manage the parking situation and the flow of traffic. Or dedicated *Something* needs to be done to manage it. I recognize additional parking spots have been added, but the volume of cars at the Activity Plex during prime times is significantly more than the parking lot allows.
responseFromOwnerText:
UPDATES:

The floor has been replaced and the warped areas have all been fixed. This was a tricky issue to diagnose, but the proper sealing of the subfloor has been found to be the culprit.

Regular upholstery cleaning of the hallway benches is underway, but this becomes particularly difficult during the salty winter season, and kids will be kids!

We have purchased additional parking spaces which seems to have solved this issue for the 2025-2026 season!

text:
There is so much potential for this place to be a great destination for a family with children to participate in activities. Unfortunately it is a complete disappointment and that is a huge disservice to its tenants.
• Parking is the biggest issue as the business run classes at the same time and this causes parking chaos. Coming 30 minutes early is often still not enough time as there can be an 8 to 10 car line up waiting on parking spots.
• There are now two dance schools running classes at the same time and it is those attending the dance schools that take up the most parking and hallway space (parents come in one car, grandparents in another car, relatives, etc to watch the little ones)
• The dance schools do not have a viewing space so there are couches placed in the hall for the parents/families to watch and wait and this is beyond chaotic. It can be documented by video as the hall is packed with adults and children blocking the way and blocking doorways. This for certain is a fire hazard and will be submitted to local fire department as a complaint.
• Maintenance is clearly lacking as the vinyl flooring needs repairs/replacement and is a major trip hazard and has been this way for a long time now
• The lounge area and couches are filthy. I can’t understand how these are never cleaned or replaced perhaps with leather like fabric that can be wiped down. Who wants to sit on that nasty fabric or risk bed bugs?
• While it is wonderful to have a little cafe on site, the coffee and food offerings are overpriced and underwhelming. The coffee is terrible yet is twice the price of a high end chain. Also they only offer two sandwich/wrap options (everything else is dessert) and both have bacon. How about a kosher or veg option? Perhaps this isn’t the place for cafe issues but a separate review..it is good to note though.

The businesses that are tenants here really should put more pressure on the venue to improve what clearly requires work.
responseFromOwnerText:
UPDATE: We have purchased additional parking spaces and this has been solved for the 2025-2026 season and onward!

We have implemented routine cleaning of the common area benches, including upholstery.

Vinyl floors have all been repaired and the issue causing the warping has been found and corrected!

The Gym is now gone, which has been replaced by a dance studio which has moved viewing areas into the unit, rather than in the hallway which caused congestion. This has made for a much better experience for hallway flow!

A large homeschool community in the area chose this studio for school hour classes. We are unable to attend late afternoon, evening and weekend classes and the studio offered us daytime classes. 8 homeschool families purchased memberships for 11/12 kids over $150 each and spent almost $30 a class here, more expensive than other studios in the area but our kids truly loved it and Zoe, the manager, has great energy and connection with them truly making the experience! When they are it is not a direct answer but a long drawn out, indirect explanation. In person is the only way to properly communicate with the studio.
Our group’s make up classes for sick and traveling families proved more difficult; instead, staying 30 minutes after class to finish 1.5 hours worth of work regardless of how many children (2-6) needed the make up.

Now they no longer offer our daytime (during school hours) classes! Months after the agreement was made, after 8 families purchased memberships for this option ONLY. I contacted another 4cats studio and learned our membership is for ONE location only and can not be used in other locations. I never experienced a membership that did not apply to other locations! I was informed they will not be doing homeschool classes across any location due to costs of opening the studio early? Surprising, considering how much is paid for memberships and classes.

Though the memberships were purchased on agreement for classes before 3pm we will not be receiving a refund of any kind after our classes were canceled. text:
⭐ Very Disappointing Experience at Jumbalo Playland – October 18, 2026

We hosted our daughter’s 3rd birthday party at Jumbalo Playland on October 18, 2026, and unfortunately, the overall experience was extremely disappointing.

We were promised access to the party hall at 12:15 PM, but the staff’s lack of punctuality and organization caused delays. To make matters worse, the hall we had booked was not provided to us, and we were given a different hall instead.

We were also promised dedicated assistance from two staff members, Shady and Abby, who were supposed to help us throughout our two-and-a-half-hour party. However, both were practically invisible throughout the event. They did not take the initiative to provide the assistance promised by Jumbalo Playland, including serving juices and providing plates. We had to repeatedly go to the front desk and ask the staff to come and do what was supposed to be part of the service.

What made the experience even worse was the rude and unprofessional attitude of the staff. Their lack of responsibility, initiative, and willingness to help added unnecessary stress to what should have been a special and joyful occasion for our daughter and our family.

Despite all these issues, we still paid the full amount for the play area and even tipped the server, expecting a basic level of professionalism and customer service in return.

A child’s birthday party is a special occasion that parents plan with a lot of love, time, and effort. Unfortunately, Jumbalo Playland failed to deliver the service and experience that were promised to us.

This review reflects our honest experience. I hope the management takes this feedback seriously, improves staff training and accountability, and ensures that future customers receive the service they pay for and are promised.

Based on our experience, I would not recommend Jumbalo Playland to families looking for a well-organized, stress-free birthday party experience.
responseFromOwnerText:
Thank you for your feedback. We reviewed this with our team and our records differ from your account.

Your party was booked for 12:30 PM to 2:30 PM, with an arrival time of 12:15 PM. Your group arrived at 12:00 PM. Room assignments are never guaranteed, and both party rooms are identical in size and setup.

Two hosts were assigned to your party: a lead host and a support host. Other team members also helped throughout the event. Your group's cash tip was given to the support host during the first hour of the party, which reflects the service being provided. Because your guest count went over the booking, extra plates were needed, and our team brought them as requested.

The concern raised at the door was about not receiving a specific room, which we do not guarantee.

We will discuss this further with our team and take action where required. Thank you for celebrating with us.

text:
UPDATED REVIEW: they have completely demolished this and put the most amazing play structure in place. I haven’t been here for months because of my experience before but I would like to completely change my review. Before it looked like random play equipment thrown together, and it was very overstimulating. They have completely transformed this space. My toddler was so amazed. I will definitely be returning.

I have been here a few times since it opened and I was one of the first people to visit after they opened. The vibe of this place is weird and not for young children. I would say, there is nothing to do if your child can’t walk (even the toddler area). The arcade machines are SOO unnecessarily loud and overstimulating. The change table in the women’s bathroom is almost broken and was scared changing a diaper I had to hold it up with my knee. The staff at the desk are very mundane…they’re kind of just there? I’m not sure if it’s the owner, but there is a male who kind of walks around or chats with the female staff at the front- it’s weird vibes. The music doesn’t make sense, it’s not kids music, it’s not radio music, it’s a mix between rock and “hold” music, which is also played extremely loud as well. I’ve only ever been when there’s one or two other kids, with all of the noise I actually can’t imagine being here for long periods of time with the music and the loud machines mixed with kids yelling and screaming. When they opened they had a promo and when I asked about it to possibly get a monthly pass, the guy told me he didn’t know what I was talking about ….i pointed to the page literally standing on the front desk and he shook his head and said it was wrong. How it could be wrong after the facility literally just opened its doors didn’t make sense. Overall just very MEH and lots of room for improvement. It’s not bad, and for ages 3/4 and up would have fun here but not worth bringing a younger child here.
responseFromOwnerText:
We’re sorry to hear that your experience didn’t meet expectations. We appreciate you taking the time to share detailed feedback, as it helps us understand how guests are experiencing the space.

Playtopia is designed to offer a variety of activities for different age groups, and we understand that comfort levels can vary depending on age and timing of visit. Your comments regarding the environment, facilities, and guest experience have been noted and will be shared with our team for review.

Thank you again for your input, and we hope your future visits, if you choose to return, feel more comfortable for your family.

— Team Playtopia Burlington

title: We Rock the Spectrum Kids Gym - Oakville

text:
If I could give this place 0 stars I would.

When we received a gift card for ‘We Rock the Spectrum’ we were very excited to bring my 4 year old autistic daughter to a place that (we thought) was designed to meet her needs. It was very expensive at $50 for my 2 children but we thought it would be worth it to go to a place where my daughter felt comfortable and safe. We couldn’t have been more wrong!

I was picturing a calm, quiet, sensory friendly indoor playground with autistic children playing, because that’s how it’s marketed.

Instead the place was completely filled with fully grown adult men and their wives. There were literally between 30-50 adults who had taken over the place as if it was their own private hang out place along with their big neurotypical teenagers who took over all the equipment so the little children who actually had autism couldn’t play.

The adults had ordered around 10 extra large pizzas to the place as if it was their own private living room and their teenage children were running around the play area holding their pizza and dropping it all over the floor.

My autistic toddler has a severe gluten and dairy allergy and unfortunately due to her autism she will eat things off the floor, so I spent the whole time trying to stop her eating the food they had dropped everywhere all over the play area.

The teenagers (who were all completely neurotypical) had completely taken over the swinging area and were swinging hard and fast to the point where it was dangerous and my little 4 year old got smashed in the head twice because everytime she walked past them to walk to the slide area she was knocked flying.

They were also running around and banging into her on the playground equipment and slide, pushing past her and laughing. They had taken a tube that was meant for crawling through and were taking turns jumping down the slide in it. Their parents were busy hanging out in the sensory areas and not watching their kids and the staff did nothing to stop it.

The place was sooo loud and chaotic that my daughter was getting very over stimulated and dysregulated so we tried to bring her into the ‘sensory room’. What a joke that was! Lounging on the chairs and beanbags meant for AUTISTIC CHILDREN in the sensory room was a room full of FULLY GROWN ADULT MEN, lounging around on the beanbags on their phones with their chargers plugged into the wall. My baby couldn’t even go in there because it was taken over by men who were treating it like their own private living room.

My daughter likes arts and crafts but again she couldn’t go in that room because it was full of ADULTS eating pizza, drinking coffee and hanging out like it was Starbucks.

My daughter was so overwhelmed by the noise and chaos that she just curled up in a fetal position on the floor crying. She doesn’t even do this in a regular indoor playground but this place was beyond chaotic.

When I mentioned my concerns to the staff I was told that “it’s because it’s March break”. I would expect this answer of somewhere like Flying Squirrel or a regular indoor playground but as a place that’s supposed to be for children on the spectrum I don’t think it’s acceptable because it’s false marketing.

The owner has the power to limit how many people are allowed in at a time. They could make a rule that only children with disabilities and their siblings are allowed in with one or two support adults, not a whole extended family of adults that wants to hang out.

Instead they have prioritized making money by opening it up to anyone who is paying. If this place wants to be a regular indoor playground that’s fine but then they shouldn’t market it as a place that’s safe for autistic children, because it’s the opposite.

My daughter has never been more overwhelmed and stressed out and it took a long time to calm her down afterwards. Shame on this place.

-The slides are a bit steep and you definitely want to supervise your smaller children - I went down with my son and it went pretty fast!
-The padded steps going up to the play structure are definitely starting to wear down a bit and are hard in some spots but that is me being very picky - overall easy to climb up and padded
-Lots of fun swings and the zip line is really cool, but the stairs to climb up/down to the zip line are VERY steep, and I almost fell trying to come down them. There should be a sign on them saying they are steep. Also be careful when swinging because even though the posts are padded the swings go in lots of different directions and you can bump into other swings/posts
-There is a bin to put toys that need to be sanitized (like if your toddler chews a toy) but the sign for it needs to be clearer as I couldn't find it at first
-The calm down room is nice with lots of soft beanbags and books - the fish light wasn't working/we couldn't turn it on, and the lights were a bit bright in there
Amenities:
-There are a couple bathrooms, I only went in the women's but it was clean and fairly spacious - there was a changing table with a couple extra diapers/wipes, soap and toilet paper were all filled and paper towels were stocked up
-Toys and drinks were available to buy at the front
-Tables were clean to sit at and eat snacks
Other:
-There was only one person working but it wasn't super busy and she was very nice and helped us get set up easily
-You can sign the waiver and sign up through their app which is super convenient!
We are very excited to go back :)
